paras_en: November 20, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – As AI data centers upgrade to high‑speed networking, optical‑module manufacturers also need more test equipment on their production lines. Keysight Technologies (KEYS‑US) announced that orders for its fiscal Q4 2026 grew 53% year‑over‑year to $2.339 billion, while revenue rose 41% year‑over‑year to $1.994 billion. Excluding the effects of acquisitions, disposals and currency over the past 12 months, orders and revenue grew 49% and 36% respectively. Adjusted earnings per share were $3.61, up from $1.91 a year earlier.

The upgrade to high‑speed networking drove a 73% year‑over‑year increase in commercial communications revenue to $1.145 billion, with wired‑communications revenue more than doubling. Keysight noted that optical‑module makers are using its equipment to scale production of 800 Gb and 1.6 Tb optical modules, verifying that high‑speed signals can be transmitted reliably before shipment. Such testing occurs not only during product R&D but also increases as factories expand mass production.

Keysight said 1.6 Tb optical modules are still in the early ramp‑up phase, while the next‑generation 3.2 Tb modules have already entered development. For fiscal Q1 2027, the company forecasts revenue of $2.040‑$2.060 billion, implying roughly a 28% year‑over‑year increase at the midpoint, and adjusted EPS of $3.63‑$3.69.

However, the order increase depends on the ability to deliver equipment. The CFO said the company entered the new fiscal year with a record high backlog of undelivered orders. After stripping out the natural backlog from sales growth, an additional $200‑$300 million of hardware orders are tied up by supply‑chain constraints, and current demand still exceeds the company’s shipping capacity.

items.title: 美國司法部結束反壟斷調查NextEra收購Dominion仍待多關審查
items.title_en: U.S. Department of Justice Ends Antitrust Probe; NextEra's Acquisition of Dominion Still Subject to Further Review
paras: 2026年11月20日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 美國司法部反壟斷部門11月19日表示，已決定結束對NextEra Energy(NEE-US)收購Dominion Energy(D-US)的調查。這筆5月宣布、規模約668億美元的全股票交易因此跨過一道關卡，但仍未取得完成交易所需的全部監管批准。
Dominion在維吉尼亞州北部供電，當地是全球主要資料中心聚落之一。AI資料中心擴建推升用電需求，也使電廠、輸電線與變電設備必須跟著擴充。NextEra主張，合併後可利用更大的規模與融資能力，支援Dominion在當地建設電力基礎設施。Dominion旗下公用事業仍將由當地團隊經營，並各自接受州監管。
兩家公司股東已於9月3日通過合併案。維吉尼亞州監管機關自11月17日展開聽證，預計最晚於2027年1月11日作出決定；南卡羅來納州則排定12月8日開始聽證，北卡羅來納州也須核准。聯邦層級另外包括聯邦能源監管委員會與核能管理委員會的審查。
兩家公司預計，若取得必要批准，交易可在2027年下半年完成。接下來的重點已從反壟斷調查，轉向各監管機關是否同意交易、以及會附加哪些條件。

paras_en: On November 19, the antitrust division of the U.S. Department of Justice announced that it has decided to close its investigation into NextEra Energy (NEE-US)’s purchase of Dominion Energy (D-US). The all‑stock deal, announced in May and valued at roughly $66.8 billion, therefore clears one hurdle but still lacks all of the regulatory approvals required to complete the transaction.

Dominion supplies power in northern Virginia, an area that is one of the world’s major data‑center clusters. The expansion of AI data centers is driving higher electricity demand, forcing power plants, transmission lines and substations to expand as well. NextEra argues that, after the merger, it can leverage greater scale and financing capacity to support Dominion’s construction of power infrastructure in the region. Dominion’s utility subsidiaries will continue to be run by local teams and will remain subject to state regulation.

The shareholders of both companies approved the merger on September 3. Virginia regulators began a hearing on November 17 and are expected to issue a decision no later than January 11, 2027; South Carolina has scheduled a hearing for December 8, and North Carolina must also approve the deal. At the federal level, the transaction is also subject to review by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

Both companies expect that, if the necessary approvals are obtained, the transaction could be completed in the second half of 2027. The focus now shifts from the antitrust investigation to whether the various regulators will consent to the deal and what conditions they may impose.

items.title: Anthropic上市估值衝破2兆美元！亞馬遜、Google成最大贏家 創辦人與早期VC身價暴漲
items.title_en: Anthropic’s IPO Valuation Breaks $2 Trillion! Amazon and Google Emerge as Biggest Winners, Founders and Early VCs See Massive Wealth Gains
paras: 人工智慧新創公司Anthropic (ANT-US) 11月19日在那斯達克掛牌上市，成為全球資本市場史上最受矚目的IPO之一。公司以每股83美元定價，首日開盤報111.50美元，較發行價高出34.34%，以基本股本計算市值約1.46兆美元，若採完全稀釋口徑，估值更達約2.02兆美元，盤中正式跨越2兆美元門檻。
此次IPO公開發行約9.8億股，其中約9.56億股由Anthropic發行，其餘約2365萬股由現有股東出售。以每股83美元計算，公開發行規模約813.4億美元。
此外，Anthropic同步安排約260億美元私募配售，兩部分合計交易規模約1073.4億美元，成為全球規模最大的IPO相關融資交易之一。這場上市不僅讓創辦團隊一舉躋身全球頂級科技富豪行列，也讓早期創投、亞馬遜 (Amazon) (AMZN-US) 與Google母公司Alphabet (Alphabet) (GOOGL-US) 等投資者迎來龐大帳面收益。
Anthropic成立僅五年，估值便從早期融資時的數億美元，快速攀升至接近兆美元。其股東名單也從科技富豪與風險投資機構，逐漸擴大至全球科技巨頭、主權財富基金及大型資產管理機構，反映AI產業的資本門檻正快速提高。
七位聯合創辦人是這場IPO最直接的受益者之一。執行長Dario Amodei與其妹妹、公司總裁Daniela Amodei，在IPO前分別持有約2.41億股。扣除此次IPO計畫出售的股份後，兩人分別持有約2.37億股及2.38億股，占公司股本約1.81%及1.82%。
以每股111.50美元的開盤價計算，Dario Amodei持股帳面價值約264.26億美元，Daniela Amodei則約265.37億美元。
另外五位共同創辦人Tom Brown、Jack Clark、Jared Kaplan、Sam McCandlish及Christopher Olah，持股數量也相當接近，約介於2.39億至2.41億股，每人持股帳面價值約266.49億至268.72億美元。
七位創辦人上市後合計持有約16.73億股，占公司已發行股份約12.79%，以111.50美元計算，帳面價值合計約1865.40億美元。除了持股增值，七人也計畫在IPO中各自出售約337.84萬股，按照83美元發行價計算，每人可套現約2.8億美元。
值得注意的是，創辦團隊雖然持股比例不高，卻仍掌握公司控制權。七人透過Founder LLC持有特殊的Class F股份，上市後仍將掌握公司50.1%的投票權。這項安排讓Anthropic即使引進大量外部資本，創辦人仍能主導重大決策。
Anthropic的融資歷程，也呈現出AI產業資本需求在短短五年間急速膨脹的過程。根據睿獸分析整理的融資時間軸，公司自2021年5月完成A輪1.24億美元融資後，陸續進行B輪5.8億美元、2023年多輪C系列融資，以及2024年D系列融資。
2023年期間，Anthropic先後完成C輪3億美元、C1輪3億美元、C2輪4.5億美元、C3輪1億美元、C4輪40億美元及C5輪20億美元融資。2024年則包括D輪7.5億美元、D1輪8.85億美元、D2輪4.53億美元、D3輪未披露，以及D4輪40億美元融資。
進入2025年後，融資規模進一步放大。公司1月完成D++輪10億美元融資，3月完成E輪35億美元融資，5月另有25億美元債務融資，9月則完成130億美元F輪融資，估值達1830億美元。
2026年資本熱度再度升級。2月12日，Anthropic完成300億美元Pre-G輪融資，估值達3800億美元；5月29日再完成650億美元H輪融資，估值升至9650億美元，距離兆美元估值僅一步之遙。
投資人陣容也隨著融資規模擴大而愈發多元，從早期投資人Jaan Tallinn、Facebook共同創辦人Dustin Moskovitz等科技富豪，到Spark Capital、Menlo Ventures等創投機構，再延伸至亞馬遜、Google、Lightspeed、ICONIQ、Coatue、紅杉資本及新加坡主權財富基金GIC等大型機構。
在這場IPO中，亞馬遜與Google是最重要的戰略投資者，也是持股比例最高的兩大外部股東。根據招股文件，在IPO及同步私募配售完成後，亞馬遜持有約19.21億股，占公司總股本14.7%；Google持有約17.90億股，占比13.7%。
若以每股111.50美元計算，亞馬遜持股帳面價值約2141億美元，Google則約1995億美元。根據《路透社》測算，亞馬遜過去對Anthropic提供的貸款及股權投資等資金合計約180億美元，Google相關投入約333億美元。
若以持股市值扣除上述歷史資金投入粗略估算，亞馬遜帳面浮盈約1961億美元，Google則約1662億美元。不過，兩家公司的歷史投入包含貸款、可轉換票據及股權投資等不同形式，並非全部都能直接視為股票成本，因此這些數字不等同於實際已實現投資收益。
亞馬遜還有尚未轉換的可轉換債券。若假設相關可轉債全部轉換為股份，且不考慮持股上限等限制，亞馬遜持股可能增加至約34.841億股，占擴大後總股本約23.8%，以每股111.50美元計算，潛在持股價值可達約3885億美元，對應帳面浮盈約3705億美元。
早期風險投資機構同樣收穫豐厚。Menlo Ventures是Anthropic最早期的投資者之一，自C輪起持續參與後續融資，並曾以每股3美元價格領投D輪，累計投資約10億美元。《The Information》估算，Menlo Ventures在IPO前持有Anthropic約1.5%股份，按發行價計算，持股帳面價值約225億美元，投資回報倍數約22.5倍。
最早入股的風險投資公司Spark Capital也持續參與Anthropic多輪融資，從C輪開始一路投入六輪，累計投資約7.77億美元。該公司一名合夥人同時擔任Anthropic董事。
Anthropic招股文件未披露Spark Capital的確切持股比例，但《The Information》估算，Spark關聯基金在IPO前持股約1%。若以每股83美元發行價及約1.5兆美元完全稀釋估值計算，持股帳面價值約150億美元，投資回報倍數約19.3倍。
與過去由創投機構主導的科技新創上市不同，Anthropic的股東結構中，大型科技公司占據重要位置。亞馬遜與Google不只是財務投資者，同時也是算力供應商、雲端平台及模型銷售通路，形成資本與商業利益高度交織的合作網絡。
Anthropic的商業模式，是這套資本網絡能夠持續擴大的另一個關鍵。公司在招股文件中將其定位為「Pay-for-intelligence」，也就是按智能使用量付費，主要透過兩種方式創造收入：一是向開發者及企業提供Claude模型，依照Token消耗量收費；二是透過Claude Code、Claude Cowork及Claude.ai等產品，向個人與企業收取訂閱費或使用費。
按量計費已成為Anthropic最主要的收入來源。2024年，按量計費業務貢獻2.88億美元，占總營收75%；2025年增至約38億美元，占比提高至83%；2026年前三季進一步達到263億美元，占總營收約79%。同期，訂閱業務收入為69億美元，占比約21%。
這種模式與傳統SaaS企業有所不同。傳統軟體服務通常以使用者席位、訂閱期間或合約金額計算收入，Anthropic則更直接與客戶實際消耗的模型運算資源掛鉤。企業使用Claude的頻率愈高、處理任務愈複雜，理論上就能帶來更多收入。
因此，Anthropic不必只依靠持續開發新客戶，也能透過既有客戶擴大AI應用範圍，提高單一客戶的使用量與貢獻收入。
企業客戶數據也反映出這項模式正在擴張。截至2026年9月底，過去12個月為Anthropic貢獻至少10萬美元收入的客戶超過1.19萬家，一年前僅有950多家；年貢獻收入超過100萬美元的客戶已超過1900家，其中約250家客戶年貢獻收入達到1000萬美元以上。
Anthropic希望Claude不再只是回答問題的聊天機器人，而是逐漸成為能夠持續參與工作、執行任務，甚至獨立完成部分工作的「Virtual Collaborator」，也就是虛擬協作者。若這項方向成功，公司的市場將不再局限於AI開發者及模型API客戶，還可能延伸至企業軟體、辦公協作、客戶服務及專業服務等領域。
不過，Anthropic的商業化成長仍高度依賴大型雲端平台。根據招股文件，2023年透過雲端服務商市場取得的收入占總營收11%，2024年升至32%，2025年達47%，2026年前三季則為44%。換言之，即使Anthropic已經建立Claude自有產品及API服務，仍有接近一半收入透過雲端平台銷售。
亞馬遜是這套合作模式的代表。雙方早在2023年建立戰略合作關係，亞馬遜除了提供資金，也將Claude整合至AWS企業AI服務體系。Anthropic則透過AWS取得雲端算力，並使用亞馬遜自行研發的Trainium AI晶片，雙方也針對硬體及軟體進行協同最佳化，讓Trainium更符合Claude模型訓練與推理需求。
在銷售端，Claude透過Amazon Bedrock進入AWS企業客戶採購體系。對已經使用AWS基礎設施的企業來說，可以直接在既有雲端平台上調用Claude，不必另外尋找模型供應商。
這形成一套相互依賴的商業循環：亞馬遜提供資金與算力，Anthropic藉由Claude增加模型使用量，再向亞馬遜採購更多運算資源。2026年4月，雙方進一步簽訂長期商業協議，Anthropic承諾在2026年5月至2036年4月期間，至少向亞馬遜採購1100億美元的運算與基礎設施服務。

Google則透過Google Cloud提供算力，並將Claude納入Vertex AI企業平台。另一張合作關係圖顯示，微軟 (Microsoft) (MSFT-US) 也透過Azure提供GPU算力，並藉由Microsoft Foundry、Copilot等企業產品分發或整合Claude。這代表Anthropic的模型已經進入多家大型雲端平台的商業體系，但同時也面臨與合作夥伴自有模型產品競爭的局面。
晶片供應商則是另一個重要環節。輝達 (NVIDIA) (NVDA-US) 與Anthropic進行戰略投資、晶片生態合作及聯合研發，圍繞GPU平台與Claude進行軟硬體協同最佳化；超微 (Advanced Micro Devices) (AMD-US) 則提供Instinct GPU及Helios系統，並針對Claude進行工程適配。

此外，博通 (Broadcom) (AVGO-US) 也參與相關晶片基礎設施建設，並提供設備租賃及融資支持。Anthropic的合作網絡還涵蓋美光 (Micron Technology) (MU-US) 及台積電 (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company) (TSM-US) 相關實體，顯示其資本與採購需求已延伸至晶片設計、記憶體及製造等AI供應鏈環節。
在企業應用端，Salesforce (CRM-US)、Snowflake (SNOW-US) 及埃森哲 (Accenture) (ACN-US) 等公司，則協助Claude進入企業資料與工作流程。2026年8月26日，Salesforce與Anthropic宣布擴大合作，推出Claudeforce，將Claude的推理能力與Salesforce企業客戶資料、銷售流程及業務操作結合。
透過在Claude中接入Salesforce功能，銷售人員可以直接查詢客戶資訊、分析銷售機會。Anthropic因此不必從零打造完整CRM系統，就能將Claude作為智能執行層接入既有企業軟體；Salesforce也能藉此提升自身產品的AI能力。
這張合作網絡的特殊之處，在於同一家科技公司可能同時是Anthropic的股東、算力供應商及模型銷售通路。亞馬遜、Google、微軟提供雲端資源與企業客戶渠道，輝達、AMD等公司提供晶片與系統，企業軟體公司則協助Claude進入實際工作場景。對Anthropic而言，這些合作能降低拓展市場的成本；對合作夥伴而言，則有機會從股權增值及後續算力採購中同時受益。
然而，萬億美元估值背後仍存在必須回答的問題。Anthropic在上市前一度被市場期待達到2兆美元估值，但隨著IPO接近，投資人開始重新檢視其營收成長、獲利能力及長期算力投入。公司最終以每股83美元定價，對應完全稀釋估值約1.5兆美元；上市首日以111.50美元開盤後，完全稀釋估值則升至約2.02兆美元。
若以2026年10月約810億美元的年化收入運行率計算，1.5兆美元估值相當於約18.5倍年化營收。對仍處於高速成長階段的AI公司而言，這個倍數並非完全沒有想像空間，但也意味著市場已提前反映未來數年的高速成長。
參與Anthropic IPO的投行預估，公司2026年營收將達520億至530億美元，2027年增至1350億至1370億美元，2028年進一步達到2700億至2800億美元。這代表公司必須在未來兩至三年持續擴大營收規模，才能支撐目前的高估值。
第一項挑戰是技術優勢能否延續。Claude Code讓Anthropic在AI程式設計市場建立競爭力，但Google、OpenAI及其他模型開發商也持續推出更強大的程式設計與AI Agent產品。
Anthropic認為，當Claude與企業內部軟體、資料系統及業務流程深度整合後，客戶轉換模型供應商的成本將提高。不過，企業仍可能同時採用多家模型供應商，並依照模型效能、價格及可靠度調整使用比例，因此客戶黏著度仍有待長期驗證。
第二項挑戰是算力投入。Anthropic營收快速成長，代表模型需求持續增加，但收入成長不必然意味著支出同步下降。前沿模型訓練需要大量運算資源，模型能力提升後，推理任務可能更加複雜；隨著AI Agent普及，企業調用模型的頻率與計算量也可能進一步增加。
根據招股文件，截至2026年9月底及其後簽訂的相關協議，Anthropic未來的採購與租賃承諾合計約9009億美元，其中約4516億美元預計將在2030年底前發生。如此龐大的長期支出，反映公司為了維持前沿模型競爭力，必須提前鎖定大量運算資源。
paras_en: Artificial‑intelligence startup Anthropic (ANT‑US) listed on Nasdaq on November 19, becoming one of the most watched IPOs in global capital‑market history. Priced at $83 per share, it opened at $111.50, 34.34% above the issue price, giving it a market cap of about $1.46 trillion on a basic‑share basis and roughly $2.02 trillion on a fully‑diluted basis, crossing the $2 trillion threshold during trading.

The IPO offered about 980 million shares to the public, of which roughly 956 million were issued by Anthropic and the remaining about 23.65 million were sold by existing shareholders. At $83 per share, the public‑offering size was about $81.34 billion.

In addition, Anthropic arranged a private placement of roughly $26 billion, bringing the total transaction size to about $107.34 billion, making it one of the largest IPO‑related financing deals worldwide. The listing vaulted the founding team into the ranks of the world’s top‑tech billionaires and delivered huge paper gains to early‑stage investors, Amazon (AMZN‑US) and Alphabet (GOOGL‑US) among them.

Anthropic was founded only five years ago, and its valuation has rocketed from a few hundred million dollars in early financing to nearly a trillion dollars. Its shareholder roster has expanded from tech moguls and venture‑capital firms to global tech giants, sovereign wealth funds and large asset‑management institutions, reflecting the rapidly rising capital barrier in the AI industry.

The seven co‑founders are among the most direct beneficiaries of the IPO. CEO Dario Amodei and his sister, company president Daniela Amodei, each held about 241 million shares before the offering. After accounting for the shares they sold in the IPO, they now hold roughly 237 million and 238 million shares respectively, representing about 1.81% and 1.82% of the company’s equity.
At the opening price of $111.50, Dario Amodei’s stake is worth about $26.426 billion, while Daniela Amodei’s is worth about $26.537 billion.

The other five co‑founders—Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish and Christopher Olah—hold similarly sized stakes, ranging from about 239 million to 241 million shares each, with paper values between $26.649 billion and $26.872 billion per person.

Together the seven founders own roughly 1.673 billion shares after the IPO, about 12.79% of the issued stock, worth approximately $186.540 billion at $111.50 per share. In addition to the appreciation, each founder plans to sell about 3.3784 million shares in the IPO, which at the $83 issue price would net roughly $280 million per person.

Although the founders’ ownership percentage is modest, they retain control of the company. Through Founder LLC they hold special Class F shares that give them 50.1% of the voting power after the listing, allowing them to steer major decisions despite the influx of external capital.

Anthropic’s financing history illustrates how quickly capital needs have ballooned in the AI sector over just five years. According to a timeline compiled by RuiShou Analytics, the company closed a $124 million Series A round in May 2021, followed by a $580 million Series B, multiple Series C rounds in 2023, and a Series D round in 2024.

In 2023 the company completed a $300 million C round, a $300 million C1 round, a $450 million C2 round, a $100 million C3 round, a $4 billion C4 round and a $2 billion C5 round. In 2024 it raised $750 million in a D round, $885 million in D1, $453 million in D2, an undisclosed amount in D3, and $4 billion in D4.

In 2025 the financing scale grew further. The firm closed a $1 billion D++ round in January, a $3.5 billion E round in March, a $2.5 billion debt raise in May, and a $13 billion F round in September, pushing its valuation to $183 billion.

Capital enthusiasm surged again in 2026. On February 12 Anthropic completed a $30 billion pre‑G round, valuing the company at $380 billion; on May 29 it closed a $65 billion H round, raising the valuation to $965 billion—just a step away from a trillion‑dollar valuation.

The investor base has broadened alongside the financing size, ranging from early backers such as Jaan Tallinn and Facebook co‑founder Dustin Moskovitz to venture firms like Spark Capital and Menlo Ventures, and extending to Amazon, Google, Lightspeed, ICONIQ, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC.

In the IPO, Amazon and Google were the most important strategic investors and the two largest external shareholders. According to the prospectus, after the IPO and the concurrent private placement, Amazon holds about 1.921 billion shares (14.7% of total equity) and Google holds about 1.790 billion shares (13.7%).

At $111.50 per share, Amazon’s stake is worth roughly $214.1 billion and Google’s about $199.5 billion. Reuters estimates that Amazon has previously provided about $18 billion in loans and equity investments to Anthropic, while Google’s total contribution is about $33.3 billion.

If one subtracts those historic cash infusions from the current market value of the holdings, Amazon’s paper gain is roughly $196.1 billion and Google’s about $166.2 billion. However, those historic inputs include loans, convertible notes and equity, not all of which can be treated as pure stock cost, so the figures do not represent realized investment returns.

Amazon also holds unconverted convertible bonds. Assuming all such bonds were converted to equity and ignoring any share‑cap limits, Amazon’s share count could rise to about 3.4841 billion, or roughly 23.8% of the enlarged capital base, valued at about $3.885 trillion at $111.50 per share, implying a paper gain of about $3.705 trillion.

Early‑stage venture firms also profited handsomely. Menlo Ventures, an early Anthropic backer, has participated in every round since Series C and led the D round at $3 per share, investing roughly $1 billion in total. The Information estimates Menlo owned about 1.5% of Anthropic before the IPO, giving a paper stake worth about $22.5 billion at the issue price—a 22.5‑fold return.
Spark Capital, the earliest investor, has also taken part in six financing rounds since the C round, investing about $777 million in total. One of its partners sits on Anthropic’s board.

The prospectus does not disclose Spark’s exact holding, but The Information estimates the Spark‑affiliated fund owned roughly 1% before the IPO. Using the $83 issue price and a fully‑diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion, the stake would be worth about $15 billion, a 19.3‑times return.

Unlike earlier tech IPOs dominated by venture capital, Anthropic’s shareholder structure features major tech companies prominently. Amazon and Google are not only financial investors but also providers of compute power, cloud platforms and model‑distribution channels, creating a tightly interwoven capital‑and‑commercial partnership network.

Anthropic’s business model underpins the ability of that network to expand. In its filing the company describes itself as “pay‑for‑intelligence,” charging customers based on the amount of AI usage, primarily through two revenue streams: licensing the Claude model to developers and enterprises by token consumption, and selling subscription‑or‑usage‑based products such as Claude Code, Claude Cowork and Claude.ai to individuals and businesses.

Usage‑based billing is Anthropic’s main revenue driver. In 2024, usage revenue contributed $288 million, 75% of total revenue; in 2025 it grew to about $3.8 billion, 83% of revenue; and in the first three quarters of 2026 it reached $26.3 billion, about 79% of total revenue, with subscription revenue at $6.9 billion (≈21%).

This model differs from traditional SaaS firms, which typically bill by seat, subscription term or contract value. Anthropic ties revenue directly to the actual compute resources customers consume; the more frequently and complexly a business uses Claude, the more revenue it generates theoretically.
Consequently, Anthropic does not need to rely solely on acquiring new customers; it can also expand AI usage within existing accounts, raising per‑customer consumption and contribution.

Enterprise‑customer data shows the model is scaling. By the end of September 2026, more than 11,900 customers generated at least $100 k of revenue in the prior 12 months, up from just over 950 a year earlier; over 1,900 customers contributed more than $1 million annually, including about 250 that generated over $10 million each.

Anthropic envisions Claude evolving from a question‑answer chatbot into a “Virtual Collaborator” that can continuously participate in work, execute tasks and even complete parts of jobs autonomously. If successful, the market would expand beyond AI developers and model‑API users to enterprise software, collaboration tools, customer‑service and professional‑services domains.

However, Anthropic’s commercial growth remains heavily dependent on large cloud platforms. According to the filing, cloud‑provider‑derived revenue was 11% of total in 2023, 32% in 2024, 47% in 2025, and 44% in the first three quarters of 2026—meaning nearly half of revenue still flows through cloud marketplaces despite Claude’s own product and API offerings.

Amazon exemplifies this partnership. The two firms forged a strategic alliance in 2023; Amazon not only supplied capital but also integrated Claude into its AWS Enterprise AI services. Anthropic uses AWS for compute and runs on Amazon’s Trainium AI chips, with joint hardware‑software optimizations to suit Claude’s training and inference needs.
On the sales side, Claude is available to AWS enterprise customers through Amazon Bedrock, allowing firms already on AWS to invoke Claude directly without seeking a separate model vendor.

This creates a mutually dependent business loop: Amazon provides capital and compute, Anthropic drives higher Claude usage, and Anthropic purchases more compute from Amazon. In April 2026 the parties signed a long‑term agreement under which Anthropic will buy at least $110 billion of compute and infrastructure services from Amazon between May 2026 and April 2036.

Google supplies compute via Google Cloud and embeds Claude in the Vertex AI enterprise platform. A separate diagram shows Microsoft (MSFT‑US) also providing GPU compute through Azure and distributing Claude via Microsoft Foundry, Copilot and other enterprise products. Thus Anthropic’s models are embedded across multiple major cloud ecosystems, while also competing with partners’ own model offerings.

Chip makers are another key piece. NVIDIA (NVDA‑US) has a strategic investment and joint‑development relationship with Anthropic, co‑optimizing GPU platforms and Claude; AMD (AMD‑US) provides Instinct GPUs and Helios systems, adapting them for Claude’s workloads.

Broadcom (AVGO‑US) also participates in related chip‑infrastructure projects, offering equipment leasing and financing. Anthropic’s network further includes Micron Technology (MU‑US) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM‑US), showing that its capital and procurement needs now span chip design, memory and manufacturing in the AI supply chain.

On the enterprise‑application front, Salesforce (CRM‑US), Snowflake (SNOW‑US) and Accenture (ACN‑US) help bring Claude into corporate data and workflow environments. On August 26 2026 Salesforce and Anthropic announced an expanded partnership launching “Claudeforce,” which blends Claude’s inference capabilities with Salesforce’s customer data, sales processes and operational tools.

By embedding Salesforce functionality into Claude, salespeople can query customer information and analyze opportunities directly within the AI assistant, letting Anthropic avoid building a full CRM from scratch while giving Salesforce AI‑enhanced product features.

The distinctive aspect of this network is that a single tech company can simultaneously be an Anthropic shareholder, a compute supplier and a model‑distribution channel. Amazon, Google and Microsoft provide cloud resources and enterprise channels; NVIDIA, AMD and others supply chips and systems; enterprise‑software firms help embed Claude into real‑world work. For Anthropic these collaborations lower market‑entry costs; for partners they create upside from equity appreciation and future compute purchases.

Nevertheless, a trillion‑dollar valuation still raises unanswered questions. Anthropic was once expected to reach a $2 trillion valuation before the IPO, but as the offering approached investors re‑examined revenue growth, profitability and long‑term compute spending. The company finally priced at $83 per share, implying a fully‑diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion; after opening at $111.50, the fully‑diluted valuation rose to roughly $2.02 trillion.

Using an annualized revenue run‑rate of about $81 billion in October 2026, a $1.5 trillion valuation corresponds to roughly 18.5× annual revenue. For a high‑growth AI firm this multiple leaves some room for imagination, but it also indicates the market has already priced in several years of rapid expansion.

The underwriting banks project Anthropic’s 2026 revenue at $52‑$53 billion, rising to $135‑$137 billion in 2027 and $270‑$280 billion in 2028. The company therefore must continue to scale revenue dramatically over the next two‑to‑three years to justify its lofty valuation.

The first challenge is whether its technical edge can be sustained. Claude Code gives Anthropic a foothold in the AI‑coding market, yet Google, OpenAI and other model developers are continuously launching more powerful coding and AI‑agent products.

Anthropic argues that once Claude is deeply integrated with a client’s internal software, data and workflows, switching costs to another model provider will rise. Still, enterprises may run multiple models simultaneously, adjusting usage based on performance, price and reliability, so long‑term stickiness remains to be proven.

The second challenge is compute spending. Rapid revenue growth drives higher model demand, but revenue expansion does not automatically translate into lower expense ratios. Cutting‑edge model training consumes massive compute; as model capabilities improve, inference workloads become more complex, and as AI agents proliferate, enterprise model calls may increase further.

According to the prospectus, as of the end of September 2026 and related agreements thereafter, Anthropic’s future procurement and leasing commitments total about $9.009 trillion, with roughly $4.516 trillion expected to be incurred by the end of 2030. Such massive long‑term outlays reflect the need to lock in compute resources well in advance to maintain a competitive edge in frontier AI models.

items.title: 一週內連破四道關卡！受Fed鷹派信號+AI股續跌影響　現貨金價跌破3600美元
items.title_en: Gold Prices Fall Below $3,600 an Ounce in a Week, Breaking Four Key Levels Amid Fed Hawk Signals and AI Stock Declines
paras: 國際現貨金價今(20)日在亞洲早盤交易時段跌破每盎司3600美元大關，較年初所創歷史新高5596美元已跌近2000美元，今年累計跌近36%，本周料將創下3月以來最大跌幅紀錄，因Fed釋放鷹派信號暗示將進一步升息，加上AI股票下跌也促使投資者賣黃金來彌補損失。
現貨金價今日早盤下跌1.35%至每盎司3576美元，本周累跌超過7%，日前一度觸及2025年9月以來的最低水平。與此同時，白銀價格下跌約13%。
現貨金價本周遭遇罕見連續潰敗，週一(16日)盤中跌破3900美元，兩天後又失守3800美元關口，昨(19)日跌勢加速，直線跳水進一步跌破3700美元。
芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee週四(19日)成為另一位暗示升息的聯準會官員，稱將考慮所有選項應對美國頑固的通膨。
美國通膨數據超預期後，聯準會(Fed)升息預期持續升溫。根據芝商所(CME)FedWatch最新數據，市場估12月升息1碼機率提升至96.4%，升息2碼的機率為3.6%。
升息預期也推高美債殖利率，10年期殖利率勢將追平2007年一項紀錄，當年收於5%上方天數達29天。利率和殖利率上升通常對黃金不利，因黃金本身不支付利息。此外，美元指數本週上漲0.7%，也讓以美元計價的黃金對大多數買家來說變得更昂貴。
paras_en: International spot gold fell below $3,600 per ounce in Asian early trading on the 20th, a steep drop of nearly $2,000 from the record high of $5,596 set at the beginning of the year and a year‑to‑date decline of almost 36%.  This week is expected to see the largest fall since March, as the Federal Reserve’s hawkish signals hint at further rate hikes and falling AI stocks have prompted investors to sell gold to cover losses.

Spot gold fell 1.35% to $3,576 per ounce in the morning session, a weekly decline of more than 7%, and at one point touched the lowest level since September 2025.  Silver prices fell about 13% during the same period.

Gold has experienced a rare streak of consecutive collapses this week: on Monday the 16th it fell below $3,900, two days later it slipped past the $3,800 mark, and on the 19th the decline accelerated, plunging straight below $3,700.
Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, on Thursday the 19th, became another Fed official to hint at rate hikes, saying he would consider all options to tackle stubborn U.S. inflation.

After U.S. inflation data surpassed expectations, Fed rate‑hike expectations continued to rise.  According to CME’s FedWatch, the probability of a 1‑basis‑point hike in December rose to 96.4%, while the chance of a 2‑basis‑point hike is 3.6%.

Rate‑hike expectations have also pushed U.S. Treasury yields higher, with the 10‑year yield poised to match a 2007 record, staying above 5% for 29 days that year.  Rising rates and yields are typically negative for gold, which pays no interest, and the dollar index rose 0.7% this week, making dollar‑denominated gold more expensive for most buyers.

items.title: AI 晶片管制｜美國收緊中國取得算力途徑，輝達出貨、海外租用與台積電代工受關注
items.title_en: AI Chip Controls: U.S. Tightens China’s Access to Computing Power, NVIDIA Shipments, Overseas Rentals, and TSMC Foundry Scrutiny
paras: 2026年11月20日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 美國對中國取得 AI 運算能力的管制，正從晶片出口擴大至海外資料中心和晶片代工。今年初，美國曾開放輝達 H200、AMD MI325X 等晶片申請對中出口，部分產品獲准後也陸續交貨；如今新規進一步限制中國企業透過海外租用算力，並收緊代工與封裝環節的審查。
這代表中國企業除了直接購買晶片，透過海外資料中心使用算力，或自行設計晶片、委託海外廠商生產，也都將面臨更嚴格的審查。
美國商務部今年 1 月調整出口政策，允許 H200、MI325X 等產品逐案申請出口中國。審查條件包括保障美國客戶供應、篩選買家，以及晶片出貨前在美國接受第三方檢驗。
美國眾議院外交事務委員會近日公布的資料顯示，截至 5 月 11 日，相關晶片申請量約 344 萬顆，其中約 87.99 萬顆獲得核准。騰訊及子公司獲准的數量為 15 萬顆，阿里巴巴為 7.5 萬顆，百度為 4.3 萬顆，比亞迪則為 4,000 顆。
國會公布的許可表顯示，這些獲准項目在 5 月 11 日時尚未出貨，但之後已有部分產品交付。美國商務部官員 7 月表示，少量 H200 已運往中國及香港；輝達 8 月也在財報文件中表示，已出貨部分獲准產品，但受中國方面限制，無法售出全部獲許可產品。
輝達最新法說會進一步指出，截至 10 月 25 日當季，獲許可的 Hopper 資料中心產品對中銷售額為 24 億美元；公司已停止相關出貨，下一季財測也未納入這部分業務。不過，輝達沒有公開說明停供原因，也沒有表示是否永久停止。
AMD 則在財報文件中揭露，部分 MI325 取得對中出口許可，但產品必須先送往美國檢驗，入境時還須繳納 25% 關稅，增加交易成本。公司未公布實際交付數量。
除了買晶片，中國企業也可透過海外資料中心租用運算資源。美國 11 月 19 日生效的新規，正是要加強這個環節的管制：符合特定條件的中國企業，若透過海外資料中心使用超過規定門檻的算力，相關業者須申請許可。
市場已傳出相關交易受到影響。中國 AI 公司 Moonshot 傳出取消一筆價值 1.5 億美元的印尼資料中心算力合約，原本計畫遠端使用輝達 B300 晶片。這是一筆算力服務合約，並非直接購買晶片；Moonshot 尚未公開確認。
新規也收緊晶圓代工與封裝環節對先進晶片的認定程序。市場傳出台積電與三星已暫停部分中國客戶的晶片出貨，等待許可釐清。對中國晶片設計公司而言，除了尋找晶片製造產能，也必須面對客戶產品是否符合美國管制規定的問題。
美國並未全面禁止相關晶片對中出口，但新規收緊執行與認定程序，晶片是否受到管制的確認時程也可能拉長。

paras_en: On November 20, 2026 (Yuan Analysis/Industry Data Center Report) – U.S. controls over China’s acquisition of AI computing power are expanding from chip exports to overseas data centers and chip foundries. Earlier this year, the U.S. opened applications for NVIDIA H200, AMD MI325X, and other chips for export to China, and some products were approved and subsequently delivered; the new rules now further restrict Chinese companies from renting computing power overseas and tighten review of foundry and packaging stages.

This means that Chinese firms will face stricter scrutiny not only for directly purchasing chips, but also for using overseas data centers, designing chips themselves, or contracting overseas manufacturers to produce them.

In January, the U.S. Department of Commerce adjusted export policy to allow case‑by‑case export applications for H200, MI325X, and similar products to China. Review conditions include ensuring U.S. customer supply, vetting buyers, and requiring third‑party inspection in the U.S. before shipment.

Data from the House Foreign Affairs Committee released recently shows that as of May 11, the total number of chip applications was about 3.44 million, with about 879,900 approved. Tencent and its subsidiaries received 150,000, Alibaba 75,000, Baidu 43,000, and BYD 4,000.

The congressional approval list indicates that these approved items had not yet shipped as of May 11, but some products were later delivered. A Commerce Department official said in July that a small number of H200s had been shipped to China and Hong Kong; NVIDIA also noted in its August filing that it had shipped some approved products, but restrictions from China prevented sale of all approved units.

NVIDIA’s latest earnings call further clarified that as of October 25, the approved Hopper data‑center products sold to China generated $2.4 billion in revenue; the company has halted related shipments, and the next quarter’s guidance excludes this business. NVIDIA did not disclose the reason for the halt or whether it is permanent.

AMD disclosed in its filings that some MI325 units received export approval to China, but the products must first be sent to the U.S. for inspection and must pay a 25% tariff upon entry, raising transaction costs. The company did not disclose actual delivery figures.

In addition to buying chips, Chinese firms can rent computing resources from overseas data centers. The new rules effective November 19 aim to strengthen control over this segment: Chinese companies meeting certain criteria that use more than the threshold amount of computing power via overseas data centers must apply for permission.

Market reports indicate that the new rules have impacted transactions. Chinese AI company Moonshot reportedly canceled a $150 million contract for Indonesian data‑center computing power that was to use NVIDIA B300 chips remotely. This is a service contract, not a direct chip purchase; Moonshot has not publicly confirmed the cancellation.

The new rules also tighten the identification process for advanced chips in wafer foundry and packaging stages. Rumors suggest that TSMC and Samsung have paused shipments to some Chinese customers pending clarification of approvals. For Chinese chip design firms, in addition to seeking manufacturing capacity, they must also confront whether their products comply with U.S. control regulations.

The U.S. has not imposed a blanket ban on exporting relevant chips to China, but the new rules tighten enforcement and identification procedures, potentially extending the timeline for confirming whether a chip is subject to control.

paras: ◆USD/JPY

據10月美國聯邦準備理事會(FED)會議紀錄顯示，決策者一致同意暫時維持率不變，但認為或許需要加大力度控制通貨膨脹的風險上升，並據FED理事沃勒和巴爾發表鷹派言論，而且國際貨幣基金組織(IMF)總裁格奧爾基耶娃週四稱，能源供應衝擊和人工智能(AI)需求推動全球通貨膨脹率加速升至4.7%，許多經濟體將收緊貨幣政策，強化FED再加息的基調，推動美元升至十九個月高點；此外，日本9月核心機械訂單較上年同期增13.4%不及預期，但較前月減少0.3%優於預估值，並據路透調查，多數經濟學家預估日本央行(BOJ)在12月會議宣布今年第三次升息及明年3月底前再加息一次，而且BOJ總裁植田和男向國會表示，通貨膨脹增速可能漸放緩，但名義工資穩步上漲及家庭收入增加支撐消費，並預計消費恢復溫和上升趨勢，暗示近期再升息，提供日圓支撐，美元兌日圓盤整於159.26低點。
隨後美國數據顯示上周初請失業金人數微升至20.3萬人及費城聯邦儲備銀行11月製造業指數降至正6.3，而且世界大型企業研究會公布美國10月領先指標跌0.3%遜於預期，但市場持續對FED進一步加息的押注，而且避險資金回流減弱，推升美元兌日圓至159.96高點。預估今日美元兌日圓阻力於159.60-80，支撐於158.70-90。
◆EUR/USD
昨日紐西蘭央行(RBNZ)布雷曼稱，通貨膨脹仍高於目標重點，經濟復甦進程不均衡，並據澳洲統計局公布10月就業人口減少4.35萬，為連續第二個月下降，失業率則攀升至五年新高4.9%，數據意外疲軟進一步強化澳洲央行(RBA)利率可能已見頂及下一步將降息的觀點，而且利率掉期市場目前已不再計入RBA再升息的可能性及預計明年下半年將啟動降息，衝擊澳幣及紐元走低，拖累歐元兌美元盤整於1.0954低點。

items.title_en: <New York Forex> Dollar Gains Pause as Anthropic IPO Boosts Risk Appetite, Yen Depreciates
paras: 美元週四(19日)兌多數主要貨幣回落，近期漲勢暫歇。人工智慧(AI)公司Anthropic即將掛牌，提振市場風險偏好，削弱美元買盤。不過，聯準會(Fed)官員的鷹派談話與最新會議紀錄，仍使進一步升息的預期支撐美元，美元指數維持在約19個月高點附近。
美股尾盤時段，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.2%，報103.65；歐元兌美元上漲0.2%，報1.1002美元。
美元指數本週觸及2025年4月2日以來最高水準。當時，美國總統川普宣布大規模關稅措施，引發美國資產賣壓。
美元這波漲勢始於11月10日，當時美國通膨數據高於預期，促使投資人提高對聯準會緊縮政策的押注。聯準會理事華勒(Christopher Waller)呼籲採取更積極措施對抗通膨，而10月27日至28日的會議紀錄也顯示，決策官員愈來愈擔心，可能需要進一步緊縮政策。
加拿大豐業銀行首席外匯策略師奧斯本(Shaun Osborne)表示：「美元這段時間已經漲了不少，我認為目前匯價已反映許多利多。」
他指出，美元多頭若要在短期內推升匯價，需要更強的信心或更多利多消息。他並將美元部分回落，歸因於Anthropic首次公開發行(IPO)前，市場風險情緒改善。
Anthropic的IPO定價高於原先行銷區間，帶動週四那斯達克期貨上漲，也提高市場對其上市表現的期待，重新提振AI類股投資情緒。
巴克萊分析師則認為，財政刺激與強勁的AI相關資本支出，反映美國經濟具有韌性，也意味經濟產出高於潛在水準的幅度可能擴大，利率將在更長時間內維持高檔，這些因素均有利美元。
儘管近期科技股遭到拋售，美元仍獲得資金流入支撐。德意志銀行追蹤逾100檔在美國境外註冊的指數股票型基金(ETF)發現，外國投資人過去兩週大舉逢低買進美股，買進力道為今年最強，顯示流向美股的資金也是支撐美元的重要因素。
隨著風險偏好回升、避險需求降溫，日元兌美元走貶。美元兌日元上漲0.4%，報159.905日元兌1美元，中止連續四個交易日下跌。
分析師指出，若AI相關資產再度遭到拋售，避險買盤與資金匯回日本可能支撐日元，但日元兌其他貨幣的升勢，可能比兌美元更為明顯。
澳幣兌美元則大致持平。澳洲10月就業人數連續第二個月減少，失業率升至五年高點，強化市場對當地利率可能已觸頂的看法。
三菱日聯金融集團(MUFG)資深外匯分析師 Lee Hardman表示，市場大幅上調對聯準會升息的預期，正對大宗商品價格及相關貨幣形成壓力。
瑞銀考量澳洲通膨仍高，以及勞動與房市情況惡化，將澳洲央行首次降息時間預測，由明年11月提前至8月，並將預估降息次數由兩次增加至三次。
英鎊兌美元升值0.1%，報1英鎊兌1.3162美元，但英鎊兌歐元則從20個月高點回落。投資人仍看好英國利率前景，同時對歐洲2027年多場重要選舉可能為歐元帶來的阻力保持警戒。
加密貨幣方面，受風險偏好改善帶動，比特幣上漲2.5%，報63,870美元，脫離上週日觸及的四個月低點62,026美元。

paras_en: The dollar fell against most major currencies on Thursday (the 19th), pausing its recent rally. The upcoming IPO of AI company Anthropic lifted market risk appetite and weakened dollar buying pressure. However, hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials and the latest meeting minutes still support expectations of further rate hikes, keeping the dollar index near a 19‑month high.
In the late‑day US equity session, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, slipped 0.2% to 103.65, while the euro rose 0.2% to $1.1002.
The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when President Trump announced large‑scale tariff measures that triggered selling pressure on US assets.

The current dollar rally began on November 10, when US inflation data came in above expectations, prompting investors to increase bets on tighter Fed policy. Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for more aggressive action against inflation, and the minutes from the Oct. 27‑28 meeting showed policymakers growing increasingly concerned that further tightening may be needed.

Shaun Osborne, chief FX strategist at Canada’s BMO Capital Markets, said: “The dollar has already risen a lot in recent weeks, and I think the current exchange rates already reflect much of the upside.”

He added that for dollar bulls to push rates higher in the short term they would need stronger conviction or more positive news, and he attributed the dollar’s partial pullback to improved market risk sentiment ahead of Anthropic’s IPO.
Anthropic’s IPO was priced above its initial marketing range, lifting Nasdaq futures on Thursday and raising expectations for its market debut, which revived sentiment toward AI‑related stocks.

Barclays analysts argue that fiscal stimulus and robust AI‑related capital spending show the US economy is resilient, suggesting output may be running above potential for longer, keeping rates high – a backdrop that benefits the dollar.

Despite recent tech‑stock sell‑offs, the dollar continued to attract inflows. Deutsche Bank, tracking over 100 offshore‑registered ETFs, found foreign investors bought US equities in large volumes over the past two weeks – the strongest buying this year – indicating that capital flowing into US stocks also underpins the dollar.
With risk appetite recovering and hedging demand easing, the yen weakened against the dollar. The USD/JPY rose 0.4% to 159.905 yen per dollar, ending a four‑day decline.

Analysts note that if AI‑related assets face another sell‑off, safe‑haven buying and capital returning to Japan could support the yen, but the yen’s gains against other currencies may be more pronounced than against the dollar.

The Australian dollar was roughly flat versus the US dollar. October employment in Australia fell for the second consecutive month, pushing the unemployment rate to a five‑year high and reinforcing market views that local rates may have peaked.
Lee Hardman, senior FX analyst at MUFG, said the market’s sharp upgrade of expectations for Fed rate hikes is putting pressure on commodity prices and related currencies.

UBS, considering still‑elevated Australian inflation and worsening labour and housing conditions, moved its forecast for the Reserve Bank of Australia’s first rate cut from November next year to August and increased the expected number of cuts from two to three.

The pound rose 0.1% to $1.3162, but the GBP/EUR slipped from a 20‑month peak. Investors remain bullish on UK rate prospects while staying cautious about the potential drag on the euro from several major European elections slated for 2027.
In crypto, improved risk appetite lifted Bitcoin 2.5% to $63,870, pulling it out of the four‑month low of $62,026 hit last Sunday.

觀察主要亞幣，日元貶值約0.3%，新台幣收升0.02%，星元和人民幣微幅波動不到0.05%，韓元升0.1%左右，泰銖升0.2%，而美元指數小跌近0.1%。
法人指出，聯準會內部鷹派釋出12月應考慮升息2碼的訊息，令市場風險意識持續提高，同時，後黃仁勳時代的AI投資焦慮高漲，AI估值調整壓力持續消化中。
值得留意的是，獨立新創AI Anthropic將在台灣時間今日晚上掛牌，掛牌行情成另一個左右市場信心的重要焦點。
paras_en: Taipei stock and forex markets faced double‑kill pressure. Starting today (20th), the Financial Supervisory Commission rolled out five major measures to stabilise the stock market, including re‑instating the "conditional short‑selling ban". The central bank also actively adjusted FX market volatility, ending the session at 32.942, up 0.5 points, while the turnover of Taipei foreign‑exchange brokerage firms shrank to $2.263 billion.

The New Taiwan dollar opened today at 32.96, down 1.3 points, fell to a low of 33.04, but after hitting the psychological 33‑level the decline did not deepen. In the last 15 minutes before close it turned higher, finishing at 32.942, with a daily range of 1.2 jiao.

Because turnover narrowed compared with yesterday, institutional investors interpret that the large‑scale fund‑outflow battle has eased somewhat, yet no clear bottoming signal has appeared for the Taiwan stock market. Whether the FX market can now hold the intangible 33‑level barrier remains under close market scrutiny.

Looking at major Asian currencies, the Japanese yen weakened about 0.3%, the New Taiwan dollar rose 0.02%, the Singapore dollar and the Chinese yuan fluctuated less than 0.05%, the Korean won rose roughly 0.1%, the Thai baht rose 0.2%, while the US dollar index slipped nearly 0.1%.

Institutions note that hawkish voices inside the Fed have signalled that a 20‑basis‑point rate hike should be considered in December, raising market risk awareness. At the same time, AI‑investment anxiety is soaring in the post‑Jensen Huang era, and pressure from AI valuation adjustments continues to be digested.
Worth noting is that the independent AI startup Anthropic will list tonight Taiwan time, and its debut price will become another key focus influencing market confidence.

paras: 美元週三(18日)週三走強，升至19個月來新高，受到美國聯準會(Fed)官員華勒(Christopher Waller)的鷹派談話，以及近期經濟數據影響，市場對下個月升息的預期更加確立。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)上漲0.2%，報103.78，創2025年4月以來最高。
聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)拒絕提供未來政策指引，使投資人更加依賴經濟數據，以及其他決策官員的談話，來判斷聯準會下一步動向。
華勒接受CNBC訪問時表示，如果央行希望降低通膨，就必須採取更「積極的行動」，包括在12月會議升息半個百分點，或是在會後聲明中引導市場預期，為進一步升息做好準備。
上週公布的通膨數據高於預期，使市場完全反映聯準會12月升息25個基點的預期，同時認為升息50個基點仍存在小幅可能性。芝商所(CME Group)FedWatch工具顯示，週二公布數據指出，美國10月零售銷售溫和成長，進一步強化市場對下個月升息的預期。
Monex USA駐華盛頓交易部門資深總監Juan Perez表示，「目前聯準會似乎非常堅定的準備升息，甚至可能採取更激進的升息方式。」
Perez指出，「這正是目前支撐美元走強的市場信念。」
不過，策略師也警告，美元若要延續升勢，可能需要新的利多催化因素。
Pepperstone研究策略師Dilin Wu表示，「若要推動美元從目前水準進一步顯著走高，市場可能需要開始反映2027年更為激進的升息路徑。」

In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, rose 0.2% to 103.78, the highest since April 2025.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh refused to provide forward guidance, causing investors to rely more on economic data and remarks from other policymakers to gauge the Fed’s next move.

In a CNBC interview, Waller said that if the central bank wants to bring inflation down, it must take more “aggressive action,” including a 0.5‑percentage‑point rate hike at the December meeting or guiding market expectations in the post‑meeting statement to prepare for further hikes.

Last week’s inflation data came in hotter than expected, leading the market to fully price in a 25‑basis‑point Fed hike in December while still seeing a small chance of a 50‑basis‑point increase. CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed that Tuesday’s data, which reported modest growth in U.S. retail sales for October, further reinforced expectations of a rate hike next month.
Juan Perez, senior director of Monex USA’s Washington trading desk, said, “The Fed now appears very resolute in preparing to raise rates, and may even adopt a more aggressive tightening path.”
Perez added, “That is the market belief currently underpinning the dollar’s strength.”
However, strategists warned that for the dollar to keep climbing, a new bullish catalyst may be needed.

Dilin Wu, a strategist at Pepperstone, said, “To push the dollar significantly higher from current levels, the market may need to start pricing in a more aggressive rate‑hike trajectory through 2027.”

CME’s FedWatch tool shows traders expect the Fed’s benchmark rate to be about 75 basis points higher in 12 months, landing in the 4.50%‑4.75% range. Investors will also watch later remarks from New York Fed President John Williams, Fed Governor Michael Barr, and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari to gauge the central bank’s next policy step.
The dollar’s rally has pushed other major currencies toward multi‑month lows.
The euro fell 0.2% against the dollar to $1.09735, briefly touching its lowest level since April 2025.
The pound slipped 0.3% to $1.3165, a one‑month low. Data showed Britain’s core inflation for October held steady month‑over‑month, easing market expectations of an imminent BoE rate hike.

items.title: 美股牛市還能跑多久？高盛：2027年再漲17% 標普上看8700點 但最強獲利成長階段已過
items.title_en: How Long Can the US Bull Market Run? Goldman Sachs: 17% Rise by 2027, S&P 500 Target 8,700 Points
paras: 高盛最新預測，美股牛市將延續至2027年，但回報率將較前幾年降溫，標普500指數明年底有望上看8700點，較目前水準上漲約17%，低於過去四年21%的年化報酬率。
高盛美股策略首席分析師Ben Snider在最新研究報告中表示，企業獲利成長仍是股市主要支撐，但隨著AI相關資本支出逐漸放緩，獲利增速也將回落。
Snider在報告中指出，標普成分股企業獲利增速將從2026年的30%降至2027年的18%，並可能持續放緩至2028年。「我們預估，隨著企業獲利成長放緩，2027年股票回報率也將有所回落。」
儘管如此，高盛認為目前美股估值仍屬合理。標普今年來持續刷新歷史高點，企業獲利快速成長使本益比倍數下降，目前指數預期本益比約18倍，待第三季財報全數公布後，標普500成分股企業可望連三季實現超過25%的獲利增長。
不過，2027年市場仍面臨兩大壓力：利率可能進一步走升，以及AI投資前景的不確定性，兩者皆可能限制股價上行空間。
Snider指出，企業獲利前景是2027年美股展望的最大變數。在悲觀情境下，若標普獲利預期回落至過去30年趨勢水準，同時本益比降至30年平均17倍，可能下跌約23%至5600點附近。反之，若AI資本支出週期比預期更強勁，或生產率成長超乎預期，推動獲利前景進一步改善，標普到2027年底可望上漲近30%至9400點。AI投資的持續性與實際回報，將決定下一階段美股表現。
產業配置上，高盛預估超大規模雲端企業將繼續受惠AI投資週期，長期大規模回購股票的「回購貴族」也有望表現突出。
值得注意的是，能源基礎設施供應商可能成為2027年獲利增長加速最明顯的群體之一，隨著AI相關基建持續推進，這類企業獲利前景可望改善。
此外，高盛建議關注醫療保健與必需消費品行業，這些類股能提供不同於科技股的配置選擇，在市場波動加劇時發揮分散風險的作用。
根據高盛判斷，2027年美股仍有望延續牛市，但驅動力將從AI資本開支帶動的高速增長，轉向更廣泛的企業獲利改善。對投資人而言，AI熱潮能否真正轉化為生產率提升與利潤增長，將決定標普最終趨近8700點的基準目標，或是向9400點的樂觀情境邁進。
paras_en: Goldman Sachs’ latest forecast suggests the US bull market will continue until 2027, but returns will cool off compared to previous years. The S&P 500 is expected to reach about 8,700 points by the end of next year, a rise of roughly 17% from current levels, below the 21% annualized return of the past four years.

Goldman Sachs’ U.S. equity strategy chief analyst Ben Snider said in a new research report that corporate earnings growth remains the main support for the market, but as AI‑related capital spending slows, earnings growth will also decline.

Snider noted that earnings growth for S&P component companies is projected to fall from 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027, and may continue to slow into 2028. ‘We expect that as corporate earnings growth slows, the 2027 stock return rate will also decline,’ he said.

Despite this, Goldman Sachs believes current U.S. equity valuations remain reasonable. The S&P has been breaking historical highs this year, and rapid earnings growth has lowered the price‑to‑earnings multiple to about 18×. After the full Q3 earnings are released, S&P component companies could achieve more than 25% earnings growth for three consecutive quarters.
However, the market will still face two major pressures in 2027: rates could rise further, and the uncertainty around AI investment prospects could limit upside potential.

Snider pointed out that corporate earnings prospects are the biggest variable for the 2027 U.S. equity outlook. In a pessimistic scenario, if S&P earnings expectations fall to the 30‑year trend level and the P/E ratio drops to the 30‑year average of 17×, the index could fall about 23% to around 5,600 points. Conversely, if AI capital spending cycles are stronger than expected or productivity growth exceeds expectations, pushing earnings prospects further, the S&P could rise nearly 30% to 9,400 points by the end of 2027. The sustainability and actual return of AI investment will determine the next phase of U.S. equity performance.

In terms of sector allocation, Goldman Sachs expects ultra‑large cloud companies to continue benefiting from the AI investment cycle, and long‑term large‑scale share‑repurchase “buy‑back aristocrats” are also likely to perform strongly.

Notably, energy infrastructure suppliers could become one of the most obvious groups to accelerate earnings growth in 2027, as AI‑related infrastructure continues to advance and improve the earnings outlook for these firms.

Additionally, Goldman Sachs recommends paying attention to healthcare and consumer staples, as these sectors offer a different allocation choice from tech stocks and can provide risk diversification when market volatility intensifies.

According to Goldman Sachs’ assessment, the U.S. equity market can still continue its bull run in 2027, but the driving force will shift from high‑growth AI capital spending to broader corporate earnings improvement. For investors, whether the AI boom can truly translate into productivity gains and profit growth will determine whether the S&P ultimately approaches the 8,700‑point target or moves toward the optimistic 9,400‑point scenario.

items.title: 〈台幣〉33元上下拋補激烈拉扯 國家隊蹲馬步穩台股匯市
items.title_en: Around NT$33, Fierce Toss‑and‑Catch; National Team Holds Steady to Stabilize Taiwan Stocks and FX
paras: 在外資龐大的出走潮下，台北股匯市今(18)日續弱，不僅加權指數又跌破4萬點關卡，最低來到39260點，跌點超過800點，新台幣也再度見貶破33元心理大關，不過，國家隊蹲馬步有效穩盤，台股盤中又翻紅，市場密切關注33元台幣價位是否為中央銀行的容忍底線。
新台幣今日以32.83元、升值2分開出後，隨即轉弱，盤中越最越低，截至11點15分最低來到33.002元，貶幅超過0.45%，是盤中最弱的主要亞幣。
反觀韓元升值達0.4%，人民幣、日元和星元小貶0.05%上下，美元指數則反彈0.1%左右。
法人分析，國安基金於4萬點伺機進場，觀察4萬點是否形成利空測試的第二隻腳，短線上台股將在AI大環境不確定下反覆利空測試，而今日適逢台指期結算，須提防外資壓低結算，並觀察轉倉後部位變化。
paras_en: Amid a massive outflow of foreign capital, Taipei's stock and foreign exchange markets continued to weaken today (the 18th), with the weighted index falling below the 40,000‑point threshold again, dropping to a low of 39,260 points, a decline of more than 800 points. The New Taiwan dollar also slipped past the psychological NT$33 barrier again. However, the “national team” took a defensive stance and effectively steadied the market, and the Taiwan stock market turned red again during trading. The market is closely watching whether the NT$33 level is the central bank’s tolerance floor.

The New Taiwan dollar opened today at NT$32.83, up 0.02, but immediately weakened, sinking lower throughout the session. By 11:15 a.m., it fell to a low of NT$33.002, a depreciation of over 0.45%, making it the weakest major Asian currency intraday.
By contrast, the Korean won appreciated about 0.4%, while the Chinese yuan, Japanese yen and Singapore dollar each slipped roughly 0.05%, and the U.S. dollar index rebounded about 0.1%.

Corporate analysts say the National Security Fund is waiting to enter around the 40,000‑point level, watching whether a second leg of a negative test forms at that point. In the short term, Taiwan stocks will undergo repeated negative tests amid uncertainty in the AI macro environment. Today also coincides with the settlement of Taiwan index futures, so caution is needed against foreign investors pushing prices down for settlement, and positions after the roll‑over should be monitored.
